# First Law — Entanglement Entropy

Unformalized claims gathered verbatim from [wiphy.org](https://wiphy.org/) (query: “entanglement first law holography”).

claims.name: first_law_entanglement_entropy_verified
claims.statement: The first law of entanglement entropy is verified for wedge holography, and the massive fluctuations are irrelevant at first order.

sources.title: Effective Action, Spectrum and First Law of Wedge Holography

claims.name: using_holography_paper_studies_timedependent
claims.statement: Using holography, the paper studies time-dependent entanglement entropy in CFTs driven by a $t$-linear source for a conserved U(1) current or a marginal scalar operator. It shows that even when the usual first law of entanglement entropy fails, a first law for the rates of change of entanglement entropy and energy still holds.

sources.title: A First Law of Entanglement Rates from Holography

claims.name: using_holography_paper_shows_entanglement
claims.statement: Using holography, the paper shows that the entanglement entropy of a very small subsystem in excited states obeys a relationship analogous to the first law of thermodynamics. In relativistic setups, the effective temperature of this subsystem is inversely proportional to its size.

sources.title: Thermodynamical Property of Entanglement Entropy for Excited States

claims.name: using_holography_paper_computes_first
claims.statement: Using holography, the paper computes the first thermal correction to the entanglement entropy of a cap-like region in a CFT on a sphere and reproduces the field-theory result. It shows that this is an order-one effect in the large-N expansion, so quantum corrections to the holographic entanglement-entropy formula are essential, and evaluates the bulk contribution with machinery developed from entanglement-first-law derivations of linearized Einstein equations.

sources.title: Thermal Corrections to Entanglement Entropy from Holography

claims.name: using_holography_low_thermal_excitations
claims.statement: Using holography for low thermal excitations of pure AdS in higher-derivative gravity, the paper studies entanglement entropy and entanglement temperature for small subsystems. It shows that the entanglement entropy depends on the boundary CFT central charges and derives an entropy-variance-energy relation consistent with the proposed first-law-like entanglement relation, with a Fefferman-Graham framework for extending the analysis to more general excited states.

sources.title: Note on Entanglement Temperature for Low Thermal Excited States in Higher Derivative Gravity

claims.name: applying_reduced_theory_holography_authors
claims.statement: Applying the reduced theory to holography, the authors derive thermodynamics and first-order hydrodynamics, finding a temperature-independent shear viscosity to entropy density ratio. In the hyperscaling violating case, they show that the entanglement entropy violates the area law logarithmically, consistent with the presence of a Fermi surface.

sources.title: Higher-derivative scalar-vector-tensor theories: black holes, Galileons, singularity cloaking and holography

claims.name: minkowski_spacetime_holography_three_four
claims.statement: For Minkowski spacetime holography in three and four dimensions, the paper develops an entanglement-entropy prescription for special subregions by refining the three-dimensional construction and proposing a four-dimensional generalization of the Ryu-Takayanagi-type formula. Under assumptions on the holographic stress tensor, it then shows that the entanglement first law is equivalent to the bulk gravitational equations linearized around Minkowski spacetime.

sources.title: Gravitation in flat spacetime from entanglement

claims.name: wedge_holography_paper_derives_brane
claims.statement: For wedge holography, the paper derives the brane effective action in perturbative (infinite Pauli-Fierz tower) and non-perturbative (higher-derivative gravity plus matter) forms, showing that the matter sector removes the ghost problem and yields a ghost-free multi-gravity interpretation with the correct Einstein-like Weyl anomaly. It also determines the graviton spectrum under boundary choices and confirms the first law of entanglement entropy, with massive modes dropping out at first order.

sources.title: Effective Action, Spectrum and First Law of Wedge Holography
